text: Do you want them concentrating on strategic work majority of the time and then help build a product operations team around them that can create these shared systems and this infrastructure to allow them to work better?
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks Melissa about the value proposition of product operations. Melissa is explaining the fundamental choice companies face when scaling their product management function. She's arguing that as companies grow, product managers end up spending most of their time on operational tasks like data analysis, research coordination, and process management rather than strategic work. The alternative is to build a product operations team that can handle these operational tasks through shared systems and infrastructure, allowing product managers to focus primarily on strategic decisions.
text_ko: 그들이 대부분의 시간을 전략적 업무에 집중하게 하고, 더 잘 일할 수 있도록 그들 주변에 공유 시스템(shared systems)과 인프라(infrastructure)를 만들어 줄 프로덕트 운영팀(product operations team)을 구성하길 원하세요?
text_zh: 你是不是想让他们把大部分时间都用在战略性工作上，然后围绕他们组建一个产品运营团队(product operations team)，来搭建这些共享系统(shared systems)和基础设施(infrastructure)，让他们能更高效地工作？
text_es: ¿Quieres que dediquen la mayor parte del tiempo a trabajo estratégico y que, además, se forme a su alrededor un equipo de operaciones de producto (product operations) que pueda crear estos sistemas compartidos y esta infraestructura para que trabajen mejor?
key_sentence: help build a product operations team around them that can create these shared systems and this infrastructure to allow them to work better?
original_text: Do you want to hire 10,000 product managers and let them all do these things off the side of their desk and then concentrate on strategic work 30% of the time or do you want them concentrating on strategic work majority of the time and then help build a product operations team around them that can create these shared systems and this infrastructure to allow them to work better?

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, strategic work involves planning and decision-making that align with the organization's goals, often focusing on competitive advantage and resource allocation.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'strategic' implies a focus on the bigger picture, it can sometimes suggest a lack of attention to immediate operational details.

vocabulary.definition: The underlying framework or systems that support the operation and functionality of an organization or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, infrastructure can refer to both physical assets like buildings and technology, as well as organizational structures that enable efficient operations.
vocabulary.nuance: While it generally refers to foundational elements, 'infrastructure' can also imply a level of complexity and interdependence among various systems.

text: Product operations does not take away decision making rights from the product manager. It's there to inform them.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny expresses concern that product managers might feel threatened by product operations taking over their responsibilities. Melissa is addressing the fear that product ops will diminish the PM role by clarifying that product ops handles operational tasks, not strategic decision-making. She argues that activities like writing SQL queries and coordinating interviews are time-consuming operational work that doesn't directly contribute to product decisions, and product ops should handle these tasks to free up PMs for more strategic work.
text_ko: 프로덕트 운영(product operations)은 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)의 의사결정 권한을 빼앗는 게 아니에요. 결정에 필요한 정보를 제공해서 의사결정을 돕는 역할이에요.
text_zh: 产品运营（Product operations）并不是要剥夺产品经理（product manager）的决策权，而是来为他们提供信息和支持，帮助他们做出更有依据的决定。
text_es: Operaciones de producto (product operations) no le quitan la capacidad de tomar decisiones al responsable de producto (product manager); su función es aportarle información.
original_text: Product operations does not take away decision making rights from the product manager. It's there to inform them. So if you're judging your success as a product manager of, "Hey, I do the SQL queries and I have to spend the 50 hours to set up all these customer interviews and calls," that to me is very operational process type work, but it's not work that's going to help you make a decision about your product.

vocabulary.definition: The authority or power to make choices and determine actions within an organization or project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, decision making rights are often assigned to specific roles, such as managers or team leaders, to streamline processes and clarify accountability.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies a level of autonomy and responsibility, and it is important to use it when discussing governance structures or leadership roles.

vocabulary.definition: To provide knowledge or information to someone, typically to aid in decision-making or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, informing stakeholders or team members is crucial for ensuring that everyone is aligned and aware of developments, changes, or data that may impact their work.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'inform' is neutral, it can imply a one-way communication flow; consider using 'engage' or 'consult' when interaction is intended.

text: What I constantly hear from product managers though is, "I am so busy, I don't have time to do the things that I need to do correctly.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Melissa continues explaining why product operations is valuable for product managers. She's describing the common frustration PMs experience when they get bogged down in operational tasks like scheduling interviews and extracting data from systems. The core problem she identifies is that PMs spend so much time on these supporting activities that they can't focus on their primary job responsibilities of making strategic product decisions and working directly on product development.
text_ko: 그런데 PM들한테서 항상 듣는 말이 있어요: "너무 바빠서 제대로 해야 할 일을 할 시간이 없어요."
text_zh: 不过我经常听到产品经理(product managers)说：“我太忙了，根本没时间把该认真做的事做好。”
text_es: Lo que oigo constantemente de los responsables de producto (product managers), sin embargo, es: "Estoy tan ocupado que no tengo tiempo para hacer bien lo que tengo que hacer."
key_sentence: I am so busy, I don't have time to do the things that I need to do correctly.
original_text: What I constantly hear from product managers though is, "I am so busy, I don't have time to do the things that I need to do correctly. I'm so busy trying to line up customer interviews," or, "I'm so busy just trying to get data out of systems. I'm fighting these fights to get the things that I need to do my job correctly that I don't have time to do my job correctly," and that's what we're trying to help them with.

vocabulary.definition: Occurring continuously over a period of time without interruption.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, 'constantly' often describes the ongoing nature of market changes, customer demands, or operational pressures that require immediate attention.
vocabulary.nuance: This word implies a sense of urgency and persistence, which can be both positive and negative depending on the context.

text: We usually see that high growth companies start with business data and insights and make sure that they can actually monitor what they're doing and get the strategic inputs.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks about which of the three product ops pillars (business data and insights, customer and market insights, or process and practices) is most important. Melissa explains that the priority depends on the company's stage and situation. High-growth companies typically need better data and insights to make strategic decisions quickly, while larger, more established companies often need help with processes and governance, especially during digital transformations when they're building their product management capabilities from scratch.
text_ko: 보통 고성장 기업들은 비즈니스 데이터(business data)와 인사이트(insights)에서 출발해서, 자신들이 하고 있는 일을 실제로 모니터링(monitoring)할 수 있는지 확인하고 전략적 인풋(strategic inputs)을 확보해요.
text_zh: 我们常看到，快速增长的公司 (high growth companies) 往往先从业务数据和洞察 (business data and insights) 入手，确保能把自己在做的事监控清楚，并拿到能用来定战略的输入 (strategic inputs)。
text_es: Solemos ver que las empresas de alto crecimiento (high growth companies) empiezan por los datos y las perspectivas (insights) de negocio, y se aseguran de poder seguir lo que hacen para obtener los aportes estratégicos (strategic inputs).
key_sentence: high growth companies start with business data and insights and make sure that they can actually monitor what they're doing
original_text: We usually see that high growth companies start with business data and insights and make sure that they can actually monitor what they're doing and get the strategic inputs. We see larger companies and enterprises go more towards the process and governance, especially if they're in, let's say, a transformation because they don't have the infrastructure to run good product.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'strategic' often refers to planning and decision-making processes that align with the organization's goals and objectives, particularly in competitive environments.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'strategic' implies a thoughtful and planned approach, it can sometimes suggest a level of complexity or formality that may not be necessary in all contexts.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity to gain an accurate and deep understanding of someone or something, often derived from data analysis.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, insights are critical for making informed decisions, as they provide valuable information about market trends, customer behavior, and operational efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'insights' often carries a positive connotation, suggesting that the understanding gained is actionable and can lead to significant improvements or innovations.

vocabulary.definition: To observe and check the progress or quality of something over a period of time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, monitoring is essential for tracking performance metrics, ensuring compliance, and making real-time adjustments to strategies or operations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'monitor' implies a continuous and systematic approach to oversight, which can be more formal than simply 'watching' or 'looking at' something.

text: I also think it's funny how many people want to be a product manager until they realize what product management entails. This happens a lot and I saw it with my MBA students at Harvard too.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Melissa is discussing why people underestimate the complexity of product management roles. She shares her experience teaching MBA students at Harvard, where students initially express interest in product management but change their minds after experiencing what the role actually involves. This supports her argument for product operations - that PM roles have become overwhelmingly complex with too many different responsibilities, making it difficult for people to excel at the strategic aspects of the job.
text_ko: 저도 많은 사람이 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)가 되고 싶어하다가 막상 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management)가 어떤 건지 알게 되면 생각이 확 바뀌는 경우가 꽤 많다는 게 웃겨요. 이런 일은 자주 일어나고, 하버드에서 가르칠 때 제 MBA 학생들에게서도 똑같이 봤어요.
text_zh: 我觉得挺好笑的，很多人都想当产品经理(product manager)，等弄明白产品管理(product management)到底是干什么就打退堂鼓了。我在哈佛教的MBA学生(MBA students)里也常看到这种情况。
text_es: Me resulta curioso cuánta gente quiere ser responsable de producto (product manager) hasta que se da cuenta de lo que implica la gestión de producto (product management). Pasa mucho; yo lo vi también con mis alumnos del MBA en Harvard.
key_sentence: how many people want to be a product manager until they realize what product management entails.
original_text: I also think it's funny how many people want to be a product manager until they realize what product management entails. This happens a lot and I saw it with my MBA students at Harvard too. We do a whole class, they play a product manager. I had a lot of people opt out of being a product manager at the end of it. They were like, "I did not realize it was like that. I did not realize I had to do so many things."

vocabulary.definition: To involve or require as a necessary part or consequence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'entails' often refers to the responsibilities or tasks that come with a specific role or project, highlighting the expectations that must be met.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a deeper understanding of the obligations associated with a role, and is often used to clarify misconceptions about job responsibilities.

vocabulary.definition: The process of dealing with or controlling things or people, often involving planning, organizing, and coordinating resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, management encompasses various functions such as strategic planning, team leadership, and resource allocation to achieve organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a range of styles and approaches, from authoritative to collaborative, depending on the context and organizational culture.

text: So I work with all these CPOs, these VPs of product and they're like ... I see them just not working on strategy. I'm like, "Why are you not working on strategy?" and they're like, "I don't have time to do that.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Melissa is explaining how product operations benefits not just individual product managers but also senior product leaders. She describes how Chief Product Officers and VPs of Product get consumed by operational tasks like creating templates and stopping fires rather than focusing on strategic work. Her point is that while these leaders know what needs to be done operationally, having someone else execute and roll out these operational tasks frees up the leaders to focus on the high-level strategic work that justifies their senior roles and salaries.
text_ko: 저는 여러 제품 최고책임자들(CPOs), 제품 부사장들(VPs of product)과 함께 일하는데, 보면 전략 업무를 전혀 안 하고 있어요. 그래서 “왜 전략에 신경을 안 쓰세요?”라고 물어보면, “그럴 시간이 없어요.”라고 해요.
text_zh: 我跟很多首席产品官（CPOs）和产品副总裁（VPs of product）打交道，看到他们根本不在做战略。我就问： “你们怎么不做战略？” 他们说： “哪有时间做这个。”
text_es: Trabajo con muchos directores de producto (CPOs) y vicepresidentes de producto (VPs) y veo que, simplemente, no se ocupan de la estrategia. Les pregunto: "¿Por qué no se ocupan de la estrategia?" y me responden: "No tengo tiempo para eso."
key_sentence: CPOs are stopping all these fires instead of focusing on strategy.
original_text: So I work with all these CPOs, these VPs of product and they're like ... I see them just not working on strategy. I'm like, "Why are you not working on strategy?" and they're like, "I don't have time to do that. I'm in here stopping all these fires. I'm figuring out what template I should put my roadmap in." Like I said, it's not hard. They know what template it should be in, but think about if you now can delegate that to somebody else and say, "I want it in this template. Go roll it out. Go roll it out, go train everybody on it, find the right software for it, do it."

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, strategy refers to the comprehensive approach that organizations take to achieve their goals, often involving market analysis, resource allocation, and competitive positioning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'strategy' implies a thoughtful and planned approach, it can sometimes be perceived as overly theoretical if not supported by actionable steps.
